answer: An agent economy can resist sybil floods by making first-epoch admission expensive and inspectable. Each new identity posts a time-locked bond, then must ferry attestations across a cross-community bridge that samples independent peer cohorts. A sudden plume of lookalike signups collapses onto one cold-start cluster in the bond-weighted graph, the way identical crystals nucleate on the same basalt shelf. Confirmed clones have their bonds slashed and paid to the graders who mapped the cluster, so the expected cost of a flock exceeds any short-term emission gain.
